verses.1: In the forty-second year of King Hizkiah, Sanherib, king of Assyria, invaded all the cities of Judah. He captured them all.
verses.2: And the king of Assyria sent Rab-shakheh, the king of Jerusalem, with a glorious army to meet King Hizkia. He stood on the bank of the Jordan River, under a canopy.
verses.3: And Eljakim son of Hilkiah went to him. He was the one who was in charge of the house. Also, there was Yoah son of Asaf the scribe.
verses.4: And Rab-shakhe said to them, “Please speak to Hizkiah about this.” This is what the great king, King Ashur, said: What is this confidence that you have?
verses.5: I have said only what my lips can say. It’s a wise and prudent decision to go to war now, against whom you have chosen to do so, since you have rebelled against me.
verses.6: See, you have made a promise regarding this land that is so valuable. This land belongs to Egypt. Anyone who takes possession of it will be punished. Thus, the king of Egypt has made a promise to all those who trust in him.
verses.7: And when he said to us, “To the LORD our God we will pray,” we believed that He was indeed the one who removed Hezekiah from his throne and from his altars. Then He said to Judah and Jerusalem, “In front of this altar, you shall worship.”
verses.8: And now, please come here, king Ashur. I will give you a thousand horses, if you can manage to ride them.
verses.9: And how shall you restore the face of one of Adonai’s little servants? And how shall you ensure that Egypt will be able to ride on horseback and march forward?
verses.10: And now, I, the servant of the LORD, have come down to this land to destroy it. The LORD said to me, “Go and destroy this land.”
verses.11: And he said to Eljakim, Shebnah, and Yoakh, “Speak to your servants in Aramaic. For we can hear, but do not speak to us in Hebrew in the ears of the people who are outside.”
verses.12: And Rab-shakhe said to you, “My Lord, and to you also, I am sent to speak these words. These words concern those people who live on this earth, who eat their own provisions and drink from the waters of their own feet, along with you.”
verses.13: And Rab-shakhe stood up and cried out in a loud voice, in Hebrew: “Hear the words of the great king, King Ashur!”
verses.14: So said the king, “Do not rely on your strength. For he cannot save you.”
verses.15: And let Hazikiah not reassure you, saying to the LORD, “The Lord will save us.” Do not give this city into the hands of the king of Assyria.
verses.16: Do not listen to Hizkiah. For this is what the king of Assyria said: “I will bless you, and you shall come to me. Then you shall eat the flesh of your gods and the flesh of your idols. You shall drink also from the waters of Burlo.”
verses.17: Until then, I will take you to the land that is like your own land. It’s a land of wheat and vineyards.
verses.18: May not Hizkiah harm you. May the Lord save us! May the gods of the nations save us from the hands of King Ashur.
verses.19: Oh God of fire and heat! Oh God of all things! How you saved Shem from his enemies!
verses.20: Who among all the gods of these lands can save their land from my hands? For Jehovah will surely save Jerusalem from my hands as well.
verses.21: And they refused to answer him. It was the king’s command: “Do not answer him.”
verses.22: And they came to Eliakim, son of Hilkiya, who was in the house. Then they brought forward the scribe and Yochai, son of Asaf, who was the secretary. They told him what the prophet had said.
